# Rune Ulmmoor

Rune Ulmmoor is currently a Degradation Modeling Scientist at Zordra Robotics, where he focuses on enhancing lithium-ion battery longevity through advanced predictive analytics. At Zordra, Rune contributes to the FluxCore project, an automated dispatch software designed to optimize battery usage schedules, balancing revenue generation with lifespan preservation.

Rune’s career began in 2015 at EnerCell Labs, where he pioneered the company’s first high-accuracy calendar aging model for lithium-ion cells under heavy cycling conditions. This model significantly improved lifespan predictions, influencing battery management strategies across several utility-scale storage deployments. From 2019 to 2022, Rune expanded his expertise at Voltix Systems, working on dynamic degradation models integrated into grid interconnection queue simulations.

Specializing in battery chemistry behavior under intense charge-discharge cycles, Rune combines empirical data with machine learning techniques to forecast degradation pathways. His notable projects include “Project PulseWave,” which refined cycle aging estimation, and “EndureGrid,” a simulation suite for long-term performance under variable dispatch scenarios.

Rune’s working style is deeply collaborative and data-driven. He partners closely with the software engineers and field operations teams at Zordra, ensuring that degradation models translate effectively into dispatch algorithms. Known for clear communication and iterative validation, Rune fosters cross-disciplinary innovation between modeling, software development, and product deployment.
